question: Is there an executable edge, measured against real prices a bettor could have obtained?
what_we_know: The engine originates lines and tests 18 single, parlay and angle candidates; none passes all eight gates. The blocker is provenance, not a lack of candidates.
what_we_dont_know: Whether any candidate would be profitable at real, timestamped, limit-aware prices. The backtests use community closing lines that are hash-verified as files but not authenticated as bookmaker quotes.
how_to_find_out: Obtain an authenticated historical quote archive (entry and close, timestamp, bookmaker, line, limits) and re-run the full gate battery.

blocking_decision: Treating any feature as available at decision time
question: Is every feature genuinely knowable before the line moves?
what_we_know: Leakage tests cover weather imputation, season-ahead fitting, whole-week parlay selection and future lines.
what_we_dont_know: Whether an availability feature can be built that is knowable at decision time and not only at settlement. Most injury information arrives after the market reacts.
how_to_find_out: Freeze a decision-time / settlement-time feature split, assert it in code, and add a test that deletes all post-kickoff fields.

question: Do player-prop legs move together, and at what joint price?
what_we_know: A joint-distribution protocol, calculated prop lines and seven priced combo hypotheses exist. Correlation is not the same thing as an executable ticket price.
what_we_dont_know: The joint distribution of prop legs at real prices, and the actual same-game-parlay quote. Standalone-price multiplication is not sufficient and is not used.
how_to_find_out: Obtain verified prop price history and joint SGP quotes, then compute joint EV against the actual ticket price.

blocking_decision: Using injury and availability as a signal
question: How much does a missing starter actually cost, and does the market already price it?
what_we_know: A descriptive estimate exists for 2006-2018: teams starting a tier-2-or-deeper quarterback scored 19.27 points per game and allowed 24.16, against 22.99 and 21.94 with the tier-1 starter. That is a research estimate from a community roster mirror, not an official measurement, and it is not causal.
what_we_dont_know: Whether that cost is already inside the market price, and what the same effect is for defenders by position group.
how_to_find_out: Join ruling-out events to quoted-line movements before and after each event and publish the distribution.

question: Are 2nd, 3rd and 4th string defenders replacing starters, and does it move the total?
what_we_know: Position-group availability pressure is measured for the current week from the official injury report. The historical roster mirror can rank depth tiers by games started for 2006-2018.
what_we_dont_know: A historical availability series for 2020-2026, and any measurement of the market's reaction to defensive depletion.
how_to_find_out: Source a 2020-2026 depth feed, then pair depletion events with quoted totals.

question: How many trials were actually run?
what_we_know: A deflated Sharpe is computed and published, but explicitly as provisional.
what_we_dont_know: The true count of models, features, parameters and strategy variants ever tried. Without it the deflated Sharpe cannot be pinned.
how_to_find_out: Freeze a trial registry before evaluation and reconcile it against the code history.

blocking_decision: Believing the published snapshot is current
question: Is the pinned data still the current season?
what_we_know: The build is pinned to an exact upstream commit and hash-checked. An earlier audit found the pin was 108 commits behind master and that some current-week finals were blank.
what_we_dont_know: Whether the pinned snapshot still covers the current week, and what a refresh would move.
how_to_find_out: Diff the pinned schedule against the official current-week schedule and record the gap.

blocking_decision: Accepting community market values as prices
question: Were the community closing lines actually executable bookmaker offers?
what_we_know: The community archive is hash-pinned and its internal arithmetic reconciles. Its own data dictionary does not name the book.
what_we_dont_know: Whether the recorded line and odds were offered, at what limit, and by whom.
how_to_find_out: Compare a sample of rows against an operator's own settlement record for the same games.

blocking_decision: Trusting the settlement engine on conflicting rows
question: Do the conflicting outcome flags in the price file matter?
what_we_know: Three 2015 games carry an outcome flag in the price file that contradicts the score file. NFL.com Game Center confirms the score file is right; settlement uses the score file.
what_we_dont_know: Whether any other conflicting flags exist across the full history.
how_to_find_out: Extend the conflict check across all seasons rather than the three found.

question: How much of the historical record has actually been checked against an official source?
what_we_know: A 31-game NFL.com comparison was performed and matches. That is a sample.
what_we_dont_know: A full census of historical scores and pregame fields checked against an official source.
how_to_find_out: Run the comparison over the entire schedule archive and publish the match rate.

question: Who funds and custodies a reward, and is the current "research and education only" position still accurate?
what_we_know: Rewards are published as unawarded, with a no-monetary-reward rule at every tier and no funded prize pool represented as existing.
what_we_dont_know: Whether any funded prize pool would be lawful or licensed where the operator is located. No official source for that has been verified, so it is left blank rather than guessed.
how_to_find_out: The owner states a funding and custody decision, or the site continues to state that no prize exists.

question: Which exact void, push, injury-settlement and dead-heat rules apply to a given ticket?
what_we_know: One operator's published parlay push rule is cited as the settlement reference, and the settlement engine refunds pushes.
what_we_dont_know: Whether those rules generalise to other operators, other markets and other sportsbooks. One operator's terms are not universal house rules.
how_to_find_out: Record per-bookmaker, per-market settlement terms from each operator's own published rules.

question: Does the injury report's silence about a team mean the team is healthy?
what_we_know: The cited report is an update list. Four teams listed no entries and four NFL teams were absent from the page at capture time.
what_we_dont_know: The real availability of those teams. Absence from the report is not evidence of health.
how_to_find_out: Re-capture after the weekly report is finalised and join against a full roster.

blocking_decision: Stating depth tiers for the current season
question: Can a 2nd, 3rd or 4th string player be identified for the current season?
what_we_know: Quarterback tiers can be ordered by games started in the schedule archive, and the report lists a team's quarterbacks.
what_we_dont_know: Depth tiers for any other position group in 2026. The only roster source reachable here ends at 2019 and its 2019 rows carry no appearance statistics.
how_to_find_out: Source a 2020-2026 official or licensed depth feed.

question: Is there any way to replay availability for past seasons?
what_we_know: One official weekly snapshot is captured and hash-recorded.
what_we_dont_know: Any official archive of historical weekly injury reports. No archive is published.
how_to_find_out: Archive the official report weekly going forward, or reconstruct availability from official inactive lists.

question: Should the leaderboard rank by profit?
what_we_know: The published board applies eligibility first and leaves unverified performance blank. Raw profit is not published as a ranking.
what_we_dont_know: A defensible risk-adjusted rank that survives the multiplicity problem.
how_to_find_out: Build the rank from weekly returns with the same Holm correction used for significance.
